root_cause: PR #2096 validates immutable identity fields but treats the remaining persisted session object, including next_action and policy, as already trusted. It also persists only a transitional phase, not the exact pending transition input required for replay-safe recovery. Focused tests prove projection helpers rather than executing the external and Human Gate composition boundaries.
causal_chain: _load_json() proves only that the session is a JSON object and _validate_identity() checks Host, registration, request, revision, and session fingerprint.
No whole-session digest, exact-field validator, or canonical next-action equality check protects phase, runtime state, pending operation, next_action, or policy.
The Host may therefore receive a structurally impossible action loaded from mutable storage even though lower write and merge authorities remain intact.
_claim_resume() records RESUMING_* but discards the exact external event or Human decision; submit_host_result likewise does not bind the submitted result into session recovery state.
A process interruption can consequently leave an explicit claim that blocks replay but cannot be reconciled by repository code.
The five focused tests use project_runtime_action() for external/Human states and do not execute successful resume_external() or resume_human() calls through one real Starter TaskRun.
rejected_hypotheses: Rely on the JSON Schema file being present; neither read() nor _update() executes it and current tests assert only selected top-level properties.
Treat the existing write guard as sufficient; it protects mutation authority but does not make a fabricated Host action a valid transport state.
Blindly rerun STARTING or RESUMING; a crash after a Provider or Host effect but before session publication can duplicate effects.
Move recovery ownership into ChatGPT/Codex prompts; durable transition reconciliation belongs to the repository control plane.
